# PLAN — iteration 1

## Current state assessment
The baseline passes simulation and has 15 routed LUTs, 6 FFs, WNS −0.946 ns and WHS +0.167 ns, so setup timing is the blocking gate. The first reported setup path runs from `read_ptr` through distributed RAM to `out_last`; the objective is LUT reduction, but timing feasibility must come first.

## Hypothesis
Replacing the pointer-selected distributed RAM read with a three-entry shift-register FIFO should remove the read-address-to-output path and improve setup timing, at the cost of more FFs and possibly more LUTs.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the top’s transparent child instantiation with an equivalent fixed-default `WIDTH=8`, `DEPTH=3` FIFO implementation using three registered `{data,last}` entries, with the oldest tuple in entry zero and output data taken directly from that entry. On pop, shift remaining entries toward entry zero; on push, write the new tuple at the post-pop tail position, including full simultaneous pop/push. Preserve the specified combinational ready/valid behavior, synchronous reset priority, no empty bypass, stall stability, tuple ordering and all data bits; include `// @latency 1`.
